name: SHLLA'AT
description: Shlla'at is a Sudanese fishing card game in which players capture cards from the table and from opponents' capture piles. A turn continues with a new draw after each capture until no capture is made. The Arabic name means 'uprooted'.

content.text: Shlla'at is a Sudanese fishing card game in which players capture cards from the table and from opponents' capture piles. A turn continues with a new draw after each capture until no capture is made. The Arabic name means 'uprooted'.

Country/Region of Origin: Sudan
Time Period: Early 21st century
Historical Development: May have originated in Sudan; very popular there in early years of the 21st century. Fishing game with captures from table and opponents' piles.
Cultural Significance: Usually played by children, also enjoyed by adults; popular social and family game. Arabic name shlla'at (شَلَّعَت) means 'uprooted'.

Minimum Players: 2
Maximum Players: 6
Optimal Players: 4
Partnerships: Optional

Type: Standard 52-card deck
Number of Decks: 1
